newsitem.title: GERMANY: German post office wants 25 pct stake in Postbank.
newsitem.headline: German post office wants 25 pct stake in Postbank.

text.p: Post AG, the German post office, wants a 25 percent stake in Postbank AG as part-payment for future use by the bank of its nationwide network of counters, German postal minister Wolfgang Boetsch said on Tuesday.

Boetsch said he would be consulting government coalition partners on the demand, which if accepted would resolve a lengthy dispute between the two state-owned companies, both of which are due to be privatised.
Postbank itself denied a statement from Boetsch that it had already given its approval for the deal.

Under the terms of the proposal, Postbank will also pay the post office 1.1 billion marks ($728.5 million) for use of its 16,500 counters in 1997, a figure that would fall in three yearly steps of eight percent and one of 13.5 percent to 750 million marks in 2001.

The post office had previously asked for a 1997 payment of 1.49 billion marks while Postbank said it was only prepared to pay one billion. The two had until the end of last month to fins a solution or have a compromise deal imposed on them.
The agreement would allow the post office to reduce its total number of counters to around 12,000 but commit it to retaining at least 10,000 branches or agents after that.

Boetsch said German finance minister Theo Waigel had already indicated his support for the deal but opposition to the post office holding such a high stake in Postbank was seen within some parts of the government coalition.
The FDP party noted that a coalition agreement reached this summer restricted the post office initially to a 15 percent stake in the bank.
